messages.subject: RE: Inquiry of blavaan
parts:
Menglin (cc the blavaan group, in case it helps someone else):

Correct, convergence="auto" runs as long as needed to achieve convergence (as judged by Gelman-Rubin statistic).

For thinning, you can add the argument

jagcontrol=list(thin=5)

to the blavaan/bcfa/bsem/bgrowth command (where 5 is the amount by which you want to thin). I think you would only want to do thinning if you have problems holding all the samples in memory... see here:

http://doingbayesiandataanalysis.blogspot.com/2011/11/thinning-to-reduce-autocorrelation.html

Ed

Menglin,

blavaan is generally similar to lavaan, so it is best to see whether the lavaan method also works for blavaan. In particular, you have things like the std.lv argument (fix latent variance to 1) and summary(fit, standardized=TRUE).

Sent: Sunday, October 15, 2017 6:24 PM
To: Merkle, Edgar C.
Cc: bla...@googlegroups.com

1 ) By default, the factor loading of the first item on a latent factor is fixed to be 1, any way to change it (I mean freely estimate the first loading)?

2 ) Is there any approach to obtain standardized estimates like the std.all in lavaan and Mplus? or any calculation method you would recommend to get the std estimates from output? Thanks a lot!


Menglin
